title: re-run build and script isolation attacks on the formal Linux sandbox host

environment.note: Every record below was executed inside WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 with gVisor runsc. Windows-local process results are not used as runsc acceptance anywhere in this report (ADR 0002).

expected.cleanup: runsc list empty, no pid/process, no state dir, no tmpfs mount

cases.attack: fork as many children as possible from the untrusted setup.py hook (200 attempts)
cases.blocked_at: OCI pids cgroup limit enforced by runsc: the container is stopped at the limit (no in-app EAGAIN observed); the 12-child control and the 128-pid scaling control prove the boundary follows the configured limit
cases.expected: a bounded 12-child fork completes under the 64-pid limit; 16 children are stopped there but admitted at 128; the 200-attempt fork bomb is stopped, publishes no digest and is reclaimed

not_run.item: host filesystem project quota (beyond the sandbox workspace tmpfs)
not_run.why: WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 has no per-directory filesystem project quota and no quota tooling installed. This ticket verifies the product's actual disk protection: the only writable mount is a size-bounded tmpfs plus RLIMIT_FSIZE, and the fill attack really hit ENOSPC with zero guest-volume growth. A host-level project quota belongs to the F15B deployment platform.
the bundle runs with --network=none; this ticket records real TCP connect failures and a live guest-side positive control, not every protocol
ADR 0002 accepts WSL2 for acceptance only; production delivery still needs a standalone Linux host
the environment only has the dev-stub profile; no real vendor credential or endpoint exists
